references.text: In the Mosaic Law, two or three witnesses are required to establish a case, which is reflected in the attempt to find witnesses against Jesus.
David complains that false witnesses rise up against him, foreshadowing Jesus' experience.
David speaks again of evil witnesses who stand against him, parallel to Jesus' situation.
The context surrounding the verse, where the chief priests and the whole council seek false testimony against Jesus.
Mark's account of the same sequence of events, where the chief priests and the whole council seek testimony against Jesus in order to condemn him to death.
